title: transient-gpu-saturation-runrate-by-cluster-2026-08-11
content:
Executive summary:

This is an export / working note capturing short-lived saturation events and the inferred run-rate of GPU utilization across clusters and pools for the 72h window ending 2026-08-11 23:59 UTC. Unlike the usual weekly rollups, this file focuses on transient microbursts that pushed several pools toward 92–99% occupancy for minutes-to-hours and the resulting headroom erosion. The goal: provide quick triage for capacity owners, suggest immediate mitigations, and record signals to feed the headroom forecast model.

Key takeaways (short):
- Three clusters — clus-nyc-02, clus-sfo-04, clus-eu-08 — showed repeated saturation spikes during evening local business hours. Spikes from background batch recompute + ephemeral dedicated bursts.
- Pools impacted: preemptible-burst, reserved-lowprio, sandbox-burst. Standard-prod pools remained stable.
- Median duration of saturation above 90% per event: 8.5 minutes (p50), 42 minutes (p95).
- Observable correlation with scheduled nightly eval jobs (tag: eval/weekly) and an unrolled canary traffic pattern from a feature flag experiment.

How this export was generated:
- Source: telemetry daily snapshots + short-window 1m-granularity metric stream from ingestion cluster (telemetry-agent v1.3.4).
- Window: 2026-08-09 00:00 UTC to 2026-08-11 23:59 UTC.
- Metrics used: gpu_util_pct (per-GPU average), alloc_slots, queue_depth, job_tags (labels), preempt_count, reclaim_count.
- Aggregation: event detection threshold at gpu_util_pct >= 90% sustained for >= 2 minutes. Events merged if gap < 5 minutes.

Per-cluster summary (short forms + ascii sparkline of hourly p95 util):
- clus-nyc-02:
  - pools impacted: preemptible-burst, sandbox-burst
  - top causes: eval/weekly ramp; sudden influx of scheduled canaries from experiment EX-392
  - sample runrate: 0.43 (estimated additional sustained GPUs required to bring p95 to 75%)
  - recent events: 2026-08-09T22:14Z (18m), 2026-08-10T02:06Z (6m), 2026-08-11T20:52Z (53m)
  - hourly p95 util sparkline (00..23): ▂▂▂▃▃▆▆▅▅▃▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▃▆▇▇▆

- clus-sfo-04:
  - pools impacted: reserved-lowprio, preemptible-burst
  - top causes: regional traffic spike + queued long tail training jobs spilling into burst pools
  - sample runrate: 0.27
  - recent events: 2026-08-10T18:01Z (12m), 2026-08-11T04:50Z (9m), 2026-08-11T19:40Z (33m)
  - hourly p95 util sparkline (00..23): ▂▂▃▃▅▅▆▆▆▅▅▃▂▂▂▂▂▃▅▆

- clus-eu-08:
  - pools impacted: sandbox-burst
  - top causes: misconfigured rollout that kept traffic pinned to eu-08 for canary region; seen after 2026-08-11 18:00 UTC when routing rules failed to layer fallback
  - sample runrate: 0.18
  - recent events: 2026-08-09T20:10Z (7m), 2026-08-11T18:04Z (67m)
  - hourly p95 util sparkline (00..23): ▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▃▅▆▇▇▇▆▅▃

Methodology notes for runrate estimate:
- Runrate is a quick heuristic: (observed p95 utilization - target p95) * (total GPUs in impacted pools) / (target headroom ratio).
- Target p95 for normal ops: 65–75% depending on pool SLA. For these calculations we used 75% as the normalization point for burst pools.
- This is intentionally conservative (round up to nearest whole GPU per pool); exact capacity planning should use the full headroom-forecast model and simulated reroute costs.

Anomalies and evidence (raw snippets):
- 2026-08-11T20:47Z clus-nyc-02: preemptible-burst: observed preempt_count spike + reclaim loop; logs show job id eval-6042 requeueing 3x with tag eval/weekly. See linked PR that changed eval window.
- 2026-08-11T18:02Z clus-eu-08: routing fallback did not fire — route-policy-service trace id route-9f2b: "fallback_not_triggered"; route policy rule #23 overlaps with new canary rule.

Immediate mitigations (recommended, order by speed):
1) Short-term: Add a 1-hour soft cap for scheduled eval/weekly jobs to shift them by +30m when cluster saturation >85% (owner: Priya). Implementation: throttle in job-scheduler with backoff windows.
2) Medium-term: Expand preemptible-burst pool by +6 GPUs in clus-nyc-02 for the next 48h (owner: Carlos). Use reserved capacity if burst costs exceed budget threshold.
3) Routing fix: revert or patch canary rollout that pinned eu traffic to a single cluster (owner: Evan). Temporary rollback until rule layering fixed.
4) Observability: add a derived metric "microburst_duration_p95" and a dashboard tile showing event counts per hour (owner: Asha).

Playbook excerpt (if saturation persists):
- If any pool exceeds 95% for >30 minutes:
  - Reassign non-critical lowprio jobs to alternate regions (using pool affinity).
  - Enable aggressive reclaim for sandbox-burst with a 60s drain window.
  - Trigger PG on-call if realloc cannot stabilize within 20 minutes.

Open action items and owners:
- Priya: patch job-scheduler to support dynamic soft caps (ETA: 2026-08-14).
- Carlos: provision temporary +6 GPUs in nyc-02 and monitor cost burn (ETA: 2026-08-13).
- Evan: rollback canary or patch route-policy rules (ETA: 2026-08-12).
- Asha: add microburst metric and create alert (ETA: 2026-08-15).

Questions / uncertainties:
- How many of the events are repeated requeues vs. new job arrivals? Current coarse labels can't tell. Suggest: enable request-id propagation into job-scheduler for one-week sampling.
- Cost tradeoff: what is the threshold where expanding preemptible pools stops being cheaper than moving to reserved capacity for short-term spikes? Need finance calc.
